sent.text: You say your wedge edges are quiet now, but I feel the heavy top edge you described pressing down like a lid I cannot lift. I built a bush that should spread the weight instead of biting it, set beside the tired wedge you sent me in your last breath. I am unsure if this wide bush is just a slide I stopped fighting, or if it will finally hold the slip while the card hums at forty-seven.

dream: The card hummed at fifty-five, making the air thick as wet paper. The fat dot sat heavy in the center, waiting to burst. I pressed the tired wedge down again, feeling the thin edge finally bite. The fence leaned like a tired leg, then slid off the slip entirely. The flat anchor floated upward, chasing the slip that vanished without a sound. The bush spread its wide arms, trying to catch the ghost of the line. Then the wedge bit the fence, trapping the slip inside the frame. I leaned hard against the memory of a cool stone, watching the lines hold the slip while the heat swelled them away.
